title: Minimum Falling Path Sum Without Same Column
description:
# Minimum Falling Path Sum Without Same Column

Given an `n x n` integer matrix `grid`, choose exactly one element from each row. Two elements chosen from adjacent rows are not allowed to be in the same column. Return the minimum possible sum of a valid path.

A path may start in any column of the first row and end in any column of the last row. Only adjacent rows are constrained; non-adjacent rows may reuse a column.

## Example 1:

**Input:** grid = [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]]
**Output:** 13
**Explanation:** One optimal path is 1 -> 5 -> 7. The chosen columns are 0, 1, and 0, so adjacent rows never use the same column.

## Example 2:

**Input:** grid = [[7]]
**Output:** 7
**Explanation:** With one row, the path contains that single value.

## Constraints:

*   `n == grid.length == grid[i].length`
*   `1 <= n <= 200`
*   `-99 <= grid[i][j] <= 99`

solutions.name: Full Table Two Minimums DP
solutions.description:
## Approach

Let `dp[row][col]` be the minimum sum of a valid path ending at `grid[row][col]`. For each new row, find the smallest and second-smallest values in the previous DP row, then fill the current DP row from the best legal previous column.

## Key Insight

The direct recurrence asks for the minimum value among all previous columns except the current column. Keeping the two best values of the previous row makes that recurrence fast while the full table keeps every state visible for teaching.

## Complexity Analysis

Each row is scanned a constant number of times, so the time complexity is O(n^2). The full DP table uses O(n^2) space.

solutions.name: Prefix Suffix Minima DP
solutions.description:
## Approach

Keep the previous DP row and build two helper arrays: `prefixMin[col]` is the best value at or before `col`, and `suffixMin[col]` is the best value at or after `col`. For a current column, the best legal previous value is the minimum of the prefix before it and the suffix after it.

## Key Insight

Excluding one column can be handled without tracking indices: everything left of the column and everything right of the column are still legal. Prefix and suffix minima make those two ranges answerable in O(1).

## Complexity Analysis

Every row builds prefix and suffix arrays and then fills the current row, all in linear time. The total time complexity is O(n^2), and the helper arrays use O(n) space.

solutions.name: Rolling Two Minimums DP
solutions.description:
## Approach

Keep only the previous DP row. Before building the next row, find the smallest and second-smallest values in the previous row. A current column uses the previous minimum unless that minimum is in the same column; then it uses the second minimum.

## Key Insight

For each current column, all previous columns are valid except one. That means the answer is always either the global minimum from the previous row or the second minimum when the global minimum is blocked.

## Complexity Analysis

Each row is scanned twice, so the time complexity is O(n^2). The rolling array for the previous row and current row uses O(n) space.

solutions.name: In-Place Two Minimums DP
solutions.description:
## Approach

Reuse `grid` as the DP table. For each row, first locate the smallest and second-smallest DP values in the previous row, then add the best legal previous value directly into each current cell.

## Key Insight

The optimized recurrence does not require preserving the original grid values after a row has been processed. Writing DP values back into the matrix removes the extra rolling array while keeping the same two-minimum rule.

## Complexity Analysis

Each row performs a constant number of linear scans. The time complexity is O(n^2), and the extra space complexity is O(1) because the input matrix stores the DP values.
